note: Painted Low-Poly Hybrid style tokens (S15). SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for materials, palette and Firm identity — every procedural model is generated from this file, and the renderer must not carry colours of its own. Forked from the sibling project's pattern (Q41a/D46).
note_marks: Carried verbatim from the pre-pipeline MARK table in scene.js so the 7a pipeline changes HOW things are built without changing what anything means. The minimap reads the same values, so the two can never disagree.
note_body: Body colours are the PAINTED part — the part a tint never touches. Keeping them separate from marks is what lets detection state stay readable: the coat stays the coat while the state band changes colour.
note_firms: S15 palettes. Firm identity is carried by COLOUR AND SYMBOL together — colour alone fails for a colourblind player, which is the same reason the 7a silhouette pass exists.
note_terrain: The TILE look — the other half of Q41c. These were the last colours still living in the renderer: the diorama ground held them as float RGB triples in terrain3d.js, the radar held a hand-synced hex copy in minimap.js, and the building mass had a third ramp inline. Three copies of one colour language, in two colour spaces, with nothing keeping them equal. Now both surfaces read this table, and 'a candidate look is a token file' is true for tiles as well as figures. Values are the authored hex; consumers convert with a plain /255, NOT through THREE.Color — colour management would sRGB-decode them and darken the ground by a factor of five.

terrain.note_block: Building mass tone ramp. A second seeded hash draw picks a point on it, so tone and height vary independently — keying both off one value makes every tall block the same shade, which reads as authored rather than grown.

note_budget: Triangle budgets are a MOBILE constraint, not an aesthetic one. The client already runs on a phone (7b) and a busy street draws dozens of these.
note_light: Lighting IS art direction, not renderer plumbing: the low, warm key from the north-west is what makes the painted low-poly look read as evening. Keeping it in tokens means a look candidate (Q41c) can change the mood without touching scene.js.
